question.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{1}{2}$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{\pi }{3}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & 2x+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{5\pi }{3}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & 2x & =\frac{5\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi  \\ 2x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & 2x & =\frac{3\pi }{2}+2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{12}+n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{3\pi }{4}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{(1+12n)\pi }{12} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{(3+4n)\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{12}$ and $x=\frac{3\pi }{4}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{13\pi }{12}$  and $x=\frac{7\pi }{4}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{12},\,\frac{3\pi }{4},\,\frac{13\pi }{12},\,\frac{7\pi }{4}.
$$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=\frac{3\pi }{4}\cdot \frac{13\pi }{12}=\frac{13{\pi }^{2}}{16}.
$$
